text:
oncall-bot: 🚨 Alert: KV cache fill-rate spike detected on prod-cluster-3 (read-heavy) — sustained growth for 7m, error-rate on inference edge +18%

maria.g: seeing huge KV evictions and continuous-batcher latencies climbing. Long-context requests (NTK/rope) seem to correlate with length > 32k tokens.

ajay.k: confirmed — p95 token-latency up, mem pressure on worker GPUs. Pattern: sliding-window prefetch created lots of unique prefixes, KV cardinality skyrocketed.

samir.r: tagging @tess for routing & canary rollback ideas. We might need immediate throttle on sliding-window prefetch + reduce continuous-batch window.

jordan: customer impact? any 5xxs or degraded responses to hosted API keys?

lee_ops: partial — some customers seeing increased 504s and degraded streaming chunks, mostly churn on dedicated nodes with longctx models. No global 500 yet. Ticket INC-5231 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-5231

maria.g: mitigation plan: 1) disable sliding-window prefetch on prod-cluster-3 (hotfix) 2) cap continuous-batch max_batch_tokens=4096 3) enable conservative KV-eviction policy (LRU decay).

ajay.k: I can flip prefetch off on region-us-east-1 pool now. Will also add a temporary routing rule to send longctx > 16k tokens to fallback model variant without prefetch.

oncall-bot: @ajay.k has been assigned to the Pager for incident INC-5231. On-call handoff: @tess please coordinate post-hotpatch validation.

ajay.k: running command on prod-ops: 
```
# disable sliding-window prefetch for pool prod-cluster-3
redwoodctl config set pool/prod-cluster-3.prefetch.sliding_window.enabled=false --apply
# cap batch tokens
redwoodctl config set runtime.continuous_batch.max_batch_tokens=4096 --apply
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for config change (cfg-2026-03-15-ops-674). Rolling update to pool nodes.

maria.g: watching KV cardinality in metrics: now at t+2m after flip, cardinality growth rate down from +120k/s to +8k/s. Eviction rate stabilizing.

tess: enabling traffic split: 90% stable, 10% longctx-fallback. Observing client error rates on fallback. Also pinging customer success to pre-emptively notify heavy users.

customer-success-bot: Alerting top 3 customers with >2% error: acct-redwood-ai, beta-simulate, vendor-x. Email templates queued.

samir.r: temporary batch cap introduced, but we need a longer-term fix: probably a quantized KV index plus prefix dedupe for rope sliding windows. I'll open a design RFC.

jordan: do we have perf regression tracked? Is this a config regression or workload change?

maria.g: preliminary root cause: recent change to sliding-window prefetch in release 2026.03.12 increased prefetch radius for rope longctx to improve latency for cached hits — but combined with continuous-batcher and NTK-style tokenization produced high unique prefix cardinality. So it's a regression in heuristics + interaction with batching.

tess: action items for on-call handoff -> postmortem: 
- (High) Revert prefetch radius change or add amplitude cap (owner: eng-runtime)
- (High) Add KV cardinality alert with adaptive thresholds per pool (owner: eng-sre)
- (Medium) Implement prefix-level dedupe and bounded-prefix-hash for sliding-window (owner: eng-ml)
- (Medium) Add integration test that simulates NTK long-context churn (owner: devex)
- (Low) Update runbooks for hotpatch steps and customer communication templates (owner: support)

lee_ops: current status: streaming errors down from 3.4% -> 0.9% in impacted pool. No further action required for hotpatch; schedule follow-up at 30m and 4h.

ajay.k: rolling config completed at t+10m. Verifying telemetry and edge logs. Still seeing a small tail — investigating whether some cached prefixes remain sticky in the KV due to TTL miscalc.

maria.g: added a temporary TTL trim: set kv.default_ttl=600s on pool to accelerate eviction of bad prefixes. Will monitor for customer-visible regressions.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next handoff in 2h to @tess. Please update INC-5231 with timeline and mitigation notes.

samir.r: opening RFC: RFC-1282 "bounded-prefetch-and-prefix-dedupe" — links in INC-5231.

tess: customer impact summary for now: ~8% of requests to long-context models had increased latency or partial-stream dropouts during spike window (peak 12:17 UTC -> 12:29 UTC). No data exfiltration, no authorization failures. Preliminary severity: Sev2 (customer-facing degradation).

jordan: will prepare postmortem draft and include timeline, config diffs, and monitoring gaps. Assigning to @maria.g for timeline, @ajay.k for mitigation writeup, @samir.r for RFC notes.

maria.g: will attach relevant logs and the grepped prefetch configs. Example problematic config snippet we rolled back: 
```
prefetch:
  sliding_window:
    enabled: true
    radius_tokens: 65536  # recent change, causes high unique prefix cardinality for longctx
```

lee_ops: note: a potential improvement is to route very large requests to isolated nodes with increased KV shard count to avoid cross-tenant blowup. Put on backlog.

tess: leaving handoff notes in the thread. If anything regresses, page again. Otherwise will close INC-5231 after 24h observation and include mitigations in weekly ops review. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-5231 acknowledged and assigned. Current status: mitigated, monitoring.

maria.g: final note — nice catch by the anomaly detector — we should tune detector to flag prefix-cardinality slope rather than absolute KV size to catch earlier.

jordan: thanks everyone. Closing active pages. Postmortem owner: @jordan.
